主要内容: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) reported a 60% increase in the output of a key automotive semiconductor component in 2021 compared to the previous year, amid a global chip shortage. This marks a 30% increase over the 2019 pre-pandemic level. The shortage has disrupted auto production lines and also impacted consumer electronics. TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, has taken "unprecedented actions" to support automakers, including reallocating capacity to industries with high demand due to digital transformation. The company emphasized its efforts to increase production and collaborate with the automotive supply chain to address the shortage. U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo also highlighted the need for greater market transparency to resolve the issue.
